t9_adoption.description: This study investigates the change management in the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems within Moroccan companies. Focusing on a range of technological, organizational, and environmental (TOE) elements, this research aims to identify key drivers and challenges that companies face in digital transformation. Through an analysis of various case studies and empirical data, the study evaluates the roles of managerial support, employee engagement, infrastructure alignment, and proactive risk management in ensuring ERP project success. t10_SI.content:

| Title | **Navigating AI Ownership in Commercial and IP License Agreements** |
| Author(s) / organization | Author not stated; contact listed: **Chiara Portner**. Organization: **Lathrop GPM** |
| Publisher | **Lathrop GPM** |
| Publication year | **year not stated** |

- Because purely AI-generated works lacking meaningful human input may not qualify for copyright registration, agreements should include explicit ownership clauses specifying which party owns AI-generated outputs, including derivatives where applicable; some providers expressly assign ownership to the customer, while others state that the customer owns outputs or condition ownership on certain terms.
- A technology company building on a third-party model may have constrained rights to grant its customers, so upstream model-provider terms regarding outputs, training data, confidentiality, indemnity and data use must be aligned with downstream customer agreements to avoid ownership conflicts, infringement exposure and liability gaps.

| Exact page title | **Information for Authors \| MISQE \| AIS Journals - AIS eLibrary** |
| Publisher/organization | **AIS Journals / AIS eLibrary** |
| Venue scope | “The key criterion for publication in *MIS Quarterly Executive* is whether a paper provides new insights for Information Systems (IS) and business professionals engaged in IS decision-making.” |
| What it accepts | “Anyone may submit an original article to be considered for publication in *MIS Quarterly Executive* provided he or she owns the copyright to the work being submitted or is authorized by the copyright owner or owners to submit the article.” Manuscripts must not exceed **7,500 words**, must be accompanied by an **Addendum**, and must be submitted electronically via **ManuscriptCentral**. |
| Review process | Submissions are screened for review readiness by the **Editor-in-Chief** and, if assigned, the **Senior Editor**; after screening, they go to **at least, but generally no more than, two Editorial Board reviewers**. The process is typically **single-blind**, and authors receive one consensus document from the Senior Editor summarizing the review team’s conclusions rather than separate reviews from each reviewer. |

venues.content:

- **Publisher/organization:** HICSS
- **Scope and submissions:** HICSS solicits papers emphasizing advances in research and development in several areas of system sciences; each paper must be submitted to one minitrack within one of the 11 larger tracks. Papers must contain original material, must not have been previously published or submitted elsewhere, and acceptance is based on a strict peer review in a double-blind process from June through August.
- **Publication year:** Not stated.

It examines technology’s impact on strategy, operations, and the workforce; new ideas for managing innovation, fostering diversity and inclusion, and promoting sustainability; and the evolving leadership skills required to navigate uncertain times. |
| **What/how it accepts for submission** | MIT SMR publishes short essays, opinion pieces, full-length articles, and research highlights; it is looking for shorter essays and research highlights ranging from **1,000–2,500 words**. | **Review process** | Receipt of an article or proposal is acknowledged immediately upon submission. If a submission is promising, it is assigned to an editor as provisionally accepted; the editor works collaboratively with authors, while MIT SMR may edit and rewrite substantially to serve its audience of business executives. |
| **Publication year** | Not stated. The page is marked “Updated on May 22, 2026.” |

venues.title: ISACA® Journal Article Submission
venues.content:
- **Page title:** ISACA® Journal Article Submission
- **Publisher/organization:** ISACA

- **Scope and submission:** The *ISACA Journal* covers relevant, new developments and in-depth technically oriented subjects with broad appeal, focusing on practical matters; it is published six times per year and also offers Online-Exclusive articles. It accepts factual recitations of research or experiential findings, approximately 2,000–3,000 words in a Word document, with references and/or endnotes required; articles must be the author’s own creation without artificial intelligence (AI) assistance.
- **Review process:** Manuscripts are reviewed by two or more members of the *Journal* review team through a double-blind peer-review process that can take up to 8 weeks.

- **Publication year:** Not stated.
